chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Ahmad ibn Idris and Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar together narrated to us from Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya ibn Imran al-Ashari. He said: Abu Abdillah al-Razi narrated to us from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Abi Hamza from Sayf ibn Amira from Muhammad ibn Utba from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahman from his father from Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him). He said:

While I and Fatima and al-Hasan and al-Husayn were with the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and his family), he suddenly turned his face towards us and started weeping. I said: Why do you weep, O Messenger of Allah? He said: I weep because of what shall be done to you after me. I said: And what is that, O Messenger of Allah? He said: I weep over the strike on you on the side of your head, and the slapping of Fatima on her cheek, and the stabbing of al-Hasan in the thigh, and the poison which he will be given to drink, and the killing of al-Husayn. He said: So the Ahl al-Bayt all wept together. Then I said: O Messenger of Allah! Our Lord did not create us save for trial. He said: Rejoice, O Ali, for Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has confided in me that none shall love you save a believer, and none shall hold malice for you save a hypocrite.
ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet Muhammad say about the tribulations of Ahl al-Bayt and the love for Ali?
ai.summary: In this profound hadith from Al-Amali of Shaykh al-Saduq, Imam Ali (AS) narrates that the Prophet Muhammad (SAWW) wept while seated with his family, foretelling the specific tribulations each member of the Ahl al-Bayt would face after him. The Prophet then consoled Ali with a divine promise that love for Ali is a sign of true faith and hatred for him is a sign of hypocrisy. This hadith was narrated in the context of a gathering in Medina and reflects the Prophet's foreknowledge of the tragic events that would befall his household.
word_analysis: he will be given to drink
